personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

short_term.text: This week's main pollutant was PM10: particles that can penetrate and lodge deep inside the lungs, which can cause irritation and inflammation.

actions.text: Plan outdoor activity for cleaner hours (see 'Usually cleanest at this station'); WHO advises adapting the timing and location of physical activity to reduce exposure.

actions.text: Avoid going to places with heavy traffic and congested areas.

actions.text: Use clean smokeless fuels (gas or electricity) for cooking and heating, and don't burn wood, leaves or garbage.

actions.text: Consult the nearest doctor if you have breathlessness, giddiness, cough, chest discomfort or pain, or red or watery eyes.

actions.text: On Moderate days, avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion.

actions.text: If you work outdoors, take frequent water breaks between work.

notes.who: WHO 24-hour guideline levels are set at the 99th percentile, i.e. about 3-4 days a year above the level are expected even where the guideline is met [8].
